name: count-up-stat-band
display_name: Figures that count up when they come into view — without ever inventing a digit
description: A row of authored figures. Each animates from zero to its real value the first time it scrolls into view, then settles on the exact authored string. The true figure is in the DOM and on the accessible name the whole time.

automatic_triggers.when: the figure first scrolls into view (IntersectionObserver, 0.4)
automatic_triggers.outcome: it counts from zero to the authored value over ~1.1 s and then displays the authored string EXACTLY as written, character for character
automatic_triggers.evidence: behaviour.js io.unobserve after the first intersection; step() restores `original` at p=1

automatic_triggers.outcome: no animation at all; the authored value is displayed immediately

honesty_clauses.clause: the animation never invents digits — it counts only to a value that was already rendered from authored data
honesty_clauses.why: an animated number is exactly where a fabricated statistic hides most comfortably; this component's own header comment says so, and the fleet has had to strip fabricated stats twice (vonc leaderboard, vetcomparison prices)
honesty_clauses.evidence: behaviour.js parses the rendered text; there is no data source it could invent from

honesty_clauses.clause: the real figure is present for assistive technology throughout — the accessible name carries the authored value while the visible text is mid-count
honesty_clauses.evidence: live page: every [data-countup] span carries aria-label with the authored value ("10+", "~97%", "<24h", "12+")

honesty_clauses.clause: non-numeric and prefixed/suffixed figures survive verbatim ("~97%", "<24h", "10+") — a figure the parser cannot read is displayed, not dropped
honesty_clauses.evidence: behaviour.js regex ^(\D*)(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)(\D*)$ with the no-match branch restoring the original

degraded_states.when: the JS bundle fails, or IntersectionObserver is unavailable
degraded_states.outcome: the authored figures are already in the HTML and simply stand (without the observer they animate immediately rather than on view)
degraded_states.evidence: template renders real values; behaviour.js fallback branch animates all

degraded_states.outcome: initialisation runs once — an explicit flag (`window.__statBandInit`) guards it
degraded_states.why: site-wide bundles get re-evaluated; a second run would restart every count-up
